stories.title: Burlington Takes 44K SF at Bay Ridge Retail Center Development
stories.excerpt: Off-price retailer Burlington has inked a 44,070-square-foot retail lease at Century Marketplace, a new retail development coming to 458 86th Street in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, developer MCB Real Estate announced Tuesday. The site between Fourth and Fifth avenues is undergoing a $130 million mixed-use redevelopment to turn the former 14-lot Century 21 department store assemblage into a 95,000-square-foot retail center. MCB, which began the redevelopment last year, also signed a grocery story to 16,042 square feet of retail space at the property, but would not provide further details. The two leases bring the assemblage to 65 percent leased. The center is expected to open in 2028. “Century Marketplace is a huge win for Bay Ridge, breathing new life into a long-vacant site and boosting the foot traffic that keeps local small businesses thriving,” Kayla Santosuosso, who represents the area on the City Council, said in a statement. “By creating local jobs, supporting working families and energizing our streets, this project builds on our promise to make our neighborhood a safer, more affordable and lively place to live.” MCB and urban retail investment firm Osiris Ventures acquired the old Century 21 site in July 2025 for $47.5 million. The length of the Burlington lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for retail space along 86th Street in Bay Ridge was $85 per square foot last year, according to the most recent Brooklyn retail report from the Real Estate Board of New York. MCB did not disclose the names of the brokers who represented the landlord and the tenant. “Century Marketplace demonstrates MCB Real Estate’s ability to execute complex structuring while delivering high-quality, attractive retail to dense markets,” Drew Gorman, a principal at MCB, said in a statement. “By bringing together a nationally recognized specialty grocery anchor, and top national retailers like Burlington, we are reigniting a well-known co
bullets: Burlington leases 44,070 SF at Century Marketplace, Bay Ridge, Brooklyn.
MCB Real Estate $130M mixed-use redevelopment of 14-lot former Century 21 site.
Retail center 65% leased; opens 2028. Grocery anchor also signed.
stories.summary: MCB Real Estate has secured Burlington as anchor tenant for 44,070 SF at Century Marketplace, a $130 million redevelopment of a defunct Century 21 department store in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn. The project also signed a grocery tenant to 16,042 SF, bringing total occupancy to 65%. The 95,000-SF retail center is expected to open in 2028.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. Mixed-use redevelopment signals neighborhood revitalization and foot-traffic recovery in Bay Ridge, which could eventually support adjacent residential demand, but this phase is retail-focused. Watch for future residential components or pipeline projects in the submarket as retail anchors stabilize the neighborhood.

stories.title: Creation, Crow Holdings Building 700K-SF Avondale Warehouse Facility
stories.excerpt: Creation in partnership with a real estate fund advised by Crow Holdings Capital, has begun construction on Avondale Tech Center, a three-building Class-A industrial campus spanning 38 acres and totaling approximately 700,000 square feet. The three buildings range from 212,184 to 254,264 square feet and feature 36-foot clear heights. The development will include tenant-focused outdoor amenities not typically found in industrial developments, such as dedicated gathering areas for each building, a walking path encircling the campus and shared pickleball courts. The campus is designed to serve advanced manufacturing, research and development and assembly operations, with target industries including pharmaceutical development, aerospace, semiconductor manufacturing and defense contracting. LGE Design Build is both the architect and general contractor for the project. Leading leasing efforts are Riley Gilbert along with John Lydon and Kelly Royle of JLL. Completion is targeted for Q3 2027. The post Creation, Crow Holdings Building 700K-SF Avondale Warehouse Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Creation and Crow Holdings Capital building 700K SF Avondale Tech Center, 38 acres.
Three Class-A industrial buildings, 36-foot clear heights; targets pharma, aerospace, semiconductor.
Completion Q3 2027. Designed for R&D and advanced manufacturing clusters.
stories.summary: Creation, in partnership with Crow Holdings Capital, has begun construction on Avondale Tech Center, a 700,000-SF, three-building Class-A industrial campus on 38 acres. The development targets advanced manufacturing, R&D, pharma, aerospace, and semiconductor tenants with 36-foot clear heights and unusual campus amenities (pickleball courts, walking paths). Completion targeted for Q3 2027.
stories.impact: Industrial growth in Avondale signals strong demand for advanced-manufacturing and R&D employment hubs in the Phoenix metro. This type of specialized industrial cluster typically attracts high-wage technical talent, driving downstream multifamily demand in adjacent submarkets. Monitor absorption and tenant roster to identify which neighborhoods benefit from inbound worker migration and rental growth tailwinds.

stories.title: CBRE: U.S. and Canadian AI Jobs Grow 45% Year-Over-Year
stories.excerpt: The ranks of U.S. and Canadian tech talent skilled in artificial intelligence grew by 45% in the past year, with AI-related roles now accounting for nearly a third of U.S. tech-talent job listings and boosting office-leasing activity in top tech hubs, CBRE reported. The firm’s 13th annual Scoring Tech Talent report highlights the clustering of AI jobs: 37% of AI jobs in the U.S. are found in the San Francisco Bay Area, New York City, Seattle and Washington, DC, while in Canada, the concentration is even greater as Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver claim 60% of AI jobs. CBRE expects the AI industry’s momentum to benefit office markets in key hubs. That’s especially true in San Francisco, where AI companies have accounted for 30% of leasing activity, roughly 10 million square feet, since 2023. “There’s no denying that AI is reshaping the tech industry and job growth in general,” said Colin Yasukochi, executive director of CBRE’s Tech Insights Center in San Francisco. “Growth of AI jobs in the U.S. far outpaced the broader tech-talent category, which expanded by 1.8% last year even as the tech industry cut some non-AI jobs. Markets adding AI jobs are further cementing their status as tech talent capitals.” The post CBRE: U.S. and Canadian AI Jobs Grow 45% Year-Over-Year appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: U.S. and Canadian AI jobs grew 45% YoY; now ~33% of U.S. tech listings.
37% of U.S. AI jobs in SF Bay, NYC, Seattle, DC; 60% of Canadian jobs in Toronto, Montreal, Vancouver.
AI companies drove 10M SF office leasing in SF since 2023; 30% of Bay Area leasing activity.
stories.summary: CBRE reports AI-related jobs grew 45% in the past year across the U.S. and Canada, now representing nearly one-third of tech-talent job listings. AI employment is heavily concentrated in four U.S. metros (San Francisco, New York, Seattle, Washington DC) and three Canadian cities, with AI companies accounting for 30% of San Francisco office leasing and roughly 10 million SF since 2023.
stories.impact: AI job clustering in major tech hubs—especially SF, NYC, Seattle, DC—is driving office demand but NOT multifamily directly in the headline. However, the second-order effect is critical: rapid, high-wage AI talent inflow into these metros will fuel residential demand and rent growth, particularly in neighborhoods with proximity to tech clusters. Developers in these metros should front-load acquisition and underwriting in submarkets adjacent to AI company concentrations before land and construction costs reflect demand acceleration.

stories.title: PCCP, RPM Pick Up 358-Unit Arlington Multifamily Community
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between PCCP and RPM Living Investments has acquired Truman at Arlington Commons, a four-story multifamily community located at 505 E Lamar Boulevard in Arlington, TX. The property was developed and owned by The Nehemiah Company. Built in 2021, the property features 358 units with an average size of 807 square feet (sf), across floorplans ranging from 576 to 1,594 sf. The units feature 10-foot ceilings, with select units offering 14-foot ceiling heights. 4,900 square feet of ground-floor retail is occupied by Nehemiah Coffee Company. Truman at Arlington Commons is located in North Arlington, a centrally positioned pocket between Dallas and Fort Worth with direct access to Interstate 30. The location provides connectivity to Arlington’s primary employment and entertainment districts, including AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, and Texas Live!, which together attract more than 50 million visitors annually. PCCP has approximately $29.3 billion in assets under management on behalf of institutional investors . The post PCCP, RPM Pick Up 358-Unit Arlington Multifamily Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PCCP and RPM Living acquired 358-unit Truman at Arlington Commons, Arlington, TX.
Built 2021, 807 SF average; near AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field; 50M annual visitors.

stories.summary: A joint venture of PCCP and RPM Living Investments has acquired Truman at Arlington Commons, a 358-unit multifamily community in North Arlington, Texas, built in 2021 with an average unit size of 807 SF. The property is positioned between Dallas and Fort Worth with direct I-30 access and proximity to major entertainment and employment anchors (AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field) that attract over 50 million annual visitors.
stories.impact: Institutional capital flows into Arlington mid-cycle assets signal continued confidence in the DFW corridor and its job-creation trajectory. This acquisition by established operators suggests stable rental fundamentals and lower basis in a central DFW submarket. For developers, Arlington's position as a geographic and employment middle ground between Dallas and Fort Worth makes it an attractive target for new supply if major employers continue to decentralize from downtown cores.

stories.title: Urban Standard Capital Provides $27M Land Loan for 440-Unit Vail, Colo., Complex
stories.excerpt: Aptitude Development has secured $26.5 million in financing to acquire 53 acres of land that will be the site of Edwards River Park, a 440-unit residential community split between affordable apartments and for-sale townhouses and condominiums in Vail, Colo., Commercial Observer can first report. Seth Weissman’s Urban Standard Capital provided the financing, while BayBridge Real Estate Capital’s Jay Miller arranged the transaction. Jared Hutter, CEO of Aptitude Development, said in a statement that the financing deal with Urban Standard Capital required four years to complete and described the lender as “a truly nimble capital partner exactly when we needed it.” Located in Vail Valley 4 miles from the famous Beaver Creek Resort and 10 miles from the 5,300-acre Vail Ski Resort, the land for what will be Edwards River Park received entitlement approval for development from the Eagle County commissioners in July 2025, with the first phase of construction expected to begin within 12 to 18 months. The final asset will be split between 276 rental apartments, with some of these units price-capped, and 164 for-sale homes, sold as either townhouses or condominiums, with some resident-occupied, deed-restricted entities and others sold as market-rate. Charlie Brosens, partner at Urban Standard Capital, said in a statement that the new asset addresses “an acute need for workforce housing in supply-constrained mountain town economies.” Eagle County currently has a workforce housing gap that is expected to grow by 58 percent by 2035, according to the firm. In recent years, Urban Standard has financed residential developments in Aspen and Telluride, Colo.; Park City, Utah; Jackson, Calif.; Driggs, Idaho; and Lake Tahoe, Nev. “These are some of the most supply-constrained, capital-intensive housing markets in the country, and sponsors need a lending partner who understands the entitlement complexity and demand fundamentals unique to resort-adjacent communities,” said Jake Simpson, s
bullets: Urban Standard Capital provided $26.5M land loan for Edwards River Park, Vail, CO.
Aptitude Development: 440 units (mix affordable apartments and for-sale condos/townhouses); 53 acres.
Entitlement approved July 2025; construction begins in 12–18 months. 4 miles from Beaver Creek, 10 miles from Vail Ski.
stories.summary: Aptitude Development secured $26.5 million in land financing from Urban Standard Capital to acquire 53 acres in Vail, Colorado for Edwards River Park, a 440-unit mixed-tenure development (affordable apartments, townhouses, condos). The project received entitlement approval in July 2025 and construction is expected to begin within 12–18 months, positioned 4 miles from Beaver Creek Resort and 10 miles from Vail Ski Resort.
stories.impact: Resort-proximate mixed-income residential development in Vail reflects continued confidence in mountain resort markets and signals demand for both workforce housing (affordability) and for-sale luxury product (high-end second homes, investment condos). For developers in ski-adjacent markets, the 440-unit scale and 12–18 month build timeline suggest strong presales/off-plan absorption. This also indicates lender comfort with entitlement-stage mountain projects, widening financing availability in resort submarkets.

stories.title: Kidder Mathews Entering Dallas Market
stories.excerpt: Kidder Mathews is expanding into Dallas, Texas, with the addition of six brokers. Mart Martindale, Brandon Beeson, Wilson Stafford, John David Cobb, and Claire Schmeltekopf form an investment sales team, while Barrett Jones joins as a healthcare tenant advisory specialist. The move marks the firm’s first entry into Texas and expands its footprint to 20 offices across six states. The new office will serve the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex and be led by former Edge Capital Markets co-founders Mart Martindale, Brandon Beeson, and Wilson Stafford. Together with Cobb and Schmeltekopf, they have completed more than $3.5 billion in transactions and have valued more than $20 billion in assets. Their clients include KeyBank, EPR Properties Trust, Trigild, BH Properties, Argentic Investment Management, and CWCapital, to name a few. In addition, Barrett Jones joins Kidder Mathews in Dallas, specializing exclusively in healthcare tenant representation. Mart Martindale joins as Senior Vice President, Managing Director, and Shareholder. The post Kidder Mathews Entering Dallas Market appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kidder Mathews entering Dallas market with six brokers; first Texas office.
Team led by Edge Capital Markets co-founders; $3.5B transaction history.
Expands firm footprint to 20 offices across six states; DFW-focused investment sales and healthcare advisory.
stories.summary: Kidder Mathews is opening its first Texas office in Dallas with six hires, including an investment sales team and healthcare tenant specialist. The office is led by former Edge Capital Markets co-founders and brings over $3.5 billion in completed transactions and $20 billion in asset valuations. The expansion marks the firm's entry into the DFW market and expands its footprint to 20 offices across six states.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Broker expansion signals confidence in DFW market depth and capital availability, but does not directly affect supply, demand, or cost for apartment developers. Monitor: if Kidder Mathews' client roster (KeyBank, EPR Properties, CWCapital, etc.) increase multifamily acquisitions, it may signal institutional capital flows into DFW assets worth tracking.

stories.title: Knightvest Capital Acquires 1,027-Unit Round Rock Apartment Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Knightvest Capital acquired the Silicon Hills portfolio, three communities totaling 1,027 units in Round Rock, Texas. Lynd Living was the seller of the three properties. The acquired portfolio includes Enclave at La Frontera, a 411-unit community built in 2004; Lakeside at La Frontera, a 366-unit community built in 2001; and Legends Lake Creek, a 250-unit community built in 2001. Enclave and Lakeside sit adjacent to one another within the La Frontera master-planned mixed-use development in Round Rock, with Legends Lake Creek approximately six miles west in the Lakeline/Lake Creek submarket. Knightvest will implement a comprehensive renovation program, including planned improvements to the exterior, common-area amenities, and a subset of unit interiors. As part of the renovation efforts, Knightvest will rename Enclave at La Frontera to Brixton, Lakeside at La Frontera to Calder, and Legends Lake Creek to Sutton. The post Knightvest Capital Acquires 1,027-Unit Round Rock Apartment Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Knightvest Capital acquired Silicon Hills portfolio: 1,027 units across three Round Rock, TX communities.
Enclave (411U, built 2004), Lakeside (366U, built 2001), Legends Lake Creek (250U, built 2001).
Comprehensive renovation program; rebranding to Brixton, Calder, Sutton. Properties in La Frontera and Lakeline submarkets.
stories.summary: Knightvest Capital has acquired the Silicon Hills portfolio, comprising three communities totaling 1,027 units in Round Rock, Texas, all built between 2001–2004. Two properties (Enclave and Lakeside) are adjacent in the La Frontera mixed-use development; the third (Legends Lake Creek) is located six miles west in the Lakeline/Lake Creek submarket. Knightvest plans comprehensive renovations and rebranding.
stories.impact: Value-add acquisition of older garden-style stock in Round Rock signals strong rent growth fundamentals and investor confidence in the Austin-adjacent submarket. Large portfolio acquisition by institutional operator suggests high absorption of renovated units post-improvement. For developers, this validates Round Rock's appeal as a demographic and employment draw (proximity to tech firms, workforce housing demand) and suggests room for newer Class-A product if Knightvest's repositioning achieves premium rent spreads.

stories.title: New York’s 485-x Is Teaching Developers to Stay Below 100 Apartments at a Time
stories.excerpt: In New York City, 485-x is one of the few tools capable of restarting rental construction at a meaningful scale. It is also widely misunderstood because policymakers and developers experience the same incentive in fundamentally different ways. For policymakers, 485-x is a housing production program. For developers, it is a feasibility framework whose thresholds determine what can actually be financed and delivered. Understanding that divergence helps explain the first wave of filings. An analysis of 312 registrations through April 2026 shows that only three projects, or 0.9 percent, contain 100 apartments or more. The other 99.1 percent remain below 100 units, while the median project contains just 24 apartments. Nearly one-third have no more than 10 units. Lev Kimyagarov. DavidBeyda.COM 212-967-6964 Those figures require an important caveat. The registry identifies prospective applicants, not completed buildings, and filing patterns cannot prove intent in any individual project. Still, when projects repeatedly stop at 99 units across separate addresses, the aggregate signal is too consistent to ignore. From a developer’s perspective, the 100-unit line is not an administrative threshold. It is a cost boundary. Under Option A, the commonly selected 35-year exemption paired with a 20 percent affordability requirement, crossing that line brings additional labor obligations. Industry estimates suggest prevailing-wage requirements can increase hard costs by roughly 18 to 28 percent, depending on building type and labor mix. For a typical mid-rise building, that can mean another $45 to $65 per square foot, or $6 million to $12 million on a 120- to 150-unit project. At current borrowing costs and rent levels, the increase can turn a marginally financeable development into one that cannot secure capital. By contrast, dividing a site into two buildings of 70 to 99 units can preserve the tax benefit while avoiding the wage trigger, producing a stronger and more predictable pr
bullets: NYC 485-x registrations: 312 filed through April 2026; 99.1% below 100 units.
Median project 24 units; nearly one-third have ≤10 units. Only 0.9% reached 100+ units.
Regulatory threshold at 100 units drives development fragmentation; feasibility framework, not scale-up program.
stories.summary: An analysis of 312 New York City 485-x registrations through April 2026 reveals that 99.1% of projects filed contain fewer than 100 units, with a median size of just 24 units and nearly one-third containing 10 or fewer units. Only three projects (0.9%) exceed 100 units. The pattern suggests that the 100-unit threshold functions as a hard feasibility breakpoint for developers, not merely an administrative checkpoint.
stories.impact: Critical for NYC multifamily developers: the 485-x program is enabling smaller, scattered-site projects but fragmenting supply into sub-100-unit parcels. This creates an arbitrage opportunity for developers able to assemble multiple small sites or propose phased development on larger land banks that clear the feasibility line. Conversely, it indicates financing and pro-forma feasibility challenges at scale in NYC, pushing capital toward neighborhood-focused micro-projects rather than large, integrated communities. Watch for aggregation plays or conversion of existing buildings.

stories.title: Investors Are Gaining More Confidence in Office: Survey
stories.excerpt: Investment appetite for office transactions is showing signs of a revival in 2026. Preference from commercial real estate investors for office transactions reached 11 percent in the second quarter. That compares to just 4 percent in early 2025 who listed the office sector as the one with the most opportunities, according to SitusAMC’s latest ValTrends quarterly research report shared exclusively with Commercial Observer ahead of its scheduled release later this week. While office sentiment in the survey was lower than the 16 percent registered in the first quarter, overall trends within the property sector are on the upswing following years of investor confidence in the asset class hovering in the low single digits, said Peter Muoio, head of SitusAMC Insights. Muoio said more clarity on valuations is driving the renewed interest. Increased pressure on some distressed debt may also be a contributing factor behind the numbers, Muoio added. “We’ve been seeing over the past year or year and a half the office investment conditions are improving,” Muoio said. “There is renewed interest.” Part of the increased bullishness toward office investments, according to Muoio, stems from “growing optimism” with the financial feasibility of executing office conversions. The report showed that office cap rates tightened by 10 basis points (bps) in the second quarter, but remained 80 bps above their long-term average. The increasing enthusiasm for office investments in the ValTrends report is part of a more evenly split preference for property types that has been developing over the past year, according to Muoio. Multifamily remained the top-ranked asset class in the second quarter, but optimism cooled in the survey from 60 percent to 36 percent compared to the previous quarter. Muoio said the drop was likely attributed to oversupply issues, particularly in the Sun Belt, taking longer to resolve than initially anticipated. bullets: SitusAMC survey: office investment preference rose to 11% in Q2 2026 vs. 4% in early 2025.
First quarter 2026 saw 16% preference; upward trend despite sentiment still below historical norms.

stories.summary: Office investment appetite among institutional CRE investors is improving, with preference for office deals reaching 11% in Q2 2026, up from just 4% in early 2025 (and 16% in Q1 2026). Clearer valuations and increased pressure on distressed office debt are cited as drivers of the renewed interest, marking a significant shift after years of single-digit sentiment.
stories.impact: Modest relevance to multifamily developers. Office recovery signals general capital availability and institutional confidence in CRE, which can improve financing conditions for other asset classes. However, office-focused capital may crowd out multifamily capital if institutional investors allocate more dry powder to office acquisitions and conversions. Monitor: if office conversion pipelines accelerate in key multifamily metros (NYC, SF, DC), they may reduce available workforce housing supply and indirectly support rents in adjacent residential markets.

stories.title: Mexican Restaurant Santo Taco Subleases Former West Village Dig Inn Space
stories.excerpt: Santo Taco is subleasing space formerly occupied by Dig Inn in Manhattan’s West Village, Commercial Observer has learned. The Mexican food concept launched by Santiago Perez in 2025 will take over the 2,800-square-foot, street-level and below-grade space at the Steven Fuchs-owned 232 Bleecker Street at the corner of Bleecker and Carmine streets, according to ManagRE. The sublease runs until 2041. ManagRE did not disclose the asking rent in the off-market deal, but the average asking rent in nearby retail corridors in the Meatpacking District was $252 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE. Navin Bhutani of ManagRE was the sole broker in the deal, and Meerkat Development is managing the buildout of the space. Dig Inn did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Fuchs, who owns a number of properties in the West Village, could not be reached for comment. Santo Taco already has two locations at 114 Kenmare Street and 94 University Place with the new location opening next month. Perez was the CEO of Mexico City-based firm Casamata Hospitality for 10 years, managing concepts like Enrique Olvera’s Pujol as well as Cosme in the Flatiron District and Damian in Los Angeles. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Santo Taco subleases 2,800 SF former Dig Inn space, 232 Bleecker Street, West Village, NYC.
Mexican restaurant startup; sublease runs to 2041. Nearby asking rent $252/SF (Meatpacking District Q2 2026).
Santo Taco already operates two NYC locations; third opening next month in retail sublease deal.
stories.summary: Santo Taco, a Mexican food concept launched by Santiago Perez in 2025, has subleased a 2,800-SF street-level and below-grade space in Manhattan's West Village (232 Bleecker Street) formerly occupied by Dig Inn. The sublease extends to 2041; comparable retail rents in the nearby Meatpacking District averaged $252/SF in Q2 2026. This is the brand's third New York location.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact. Retail subleasing in West Village signals continued demand for food-service and hospitality tenants in high-barrier Manhattan neighborhoods, but does not affect residential supply, demand, or feasibility. Indirect signal only: strong retail leasing and new restaurant openings in premium Manhattan submarkets can support positive retail income in mixed-use multifamily developments but does not drive new residential construction decisions.
